rachel: Heads up, running into a weird typing gap in the Python SDK for streaming chat. Editor/autogen stubs mark stream() as `AsyncIterator[Union[ChatDelta, str]]` but runtime yields objects that look like TypedDicts. Mypy/pyright both complain when we try to access `chunk["delta"]["role"]`.

tom: Can you paste a minimal repro? I'm guessing Optional/Union is the culprit.

rachel: Minimal example below (mypy 1.9.0):

```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
from typing import AsyncIterator
client = AsyncClient(api_key="x")

async def stream_chat() -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    async for chunk in client.chat.stream(model="redwood/tiny", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]):
        # stub type: Union[ChatDelta, str]
        # runtime: {'delta': {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'hey'}}
        role = chunk['delta']['role']  # mypy: "Item access on Union[TypedDict, str]"
        yield role
```

rachel: Error: "Value of type "Union[TypedDict, str]" is not indexable"

arun: Ah. We generate a bare TypedDict for chat deltas in the autogen runtime (so editors show fields) but the stub uses a union with plain str for convenience (text chunks). That union makes index access unsafe.

priya: Two approaches: 1) make the stub more precise: a discriminated union like `Union[ChatDeltaTypedDict, Literal["text"]]` (ugly), or 2) expose a small helper Typed model `ChatChunk` with attributes `.delta`/`.text` so consumers use attribute access (`chunk.delta['role']`) and typing stays consistent.

tom: Adding a light wrapper type seems nicer ergonomically. Changing the stub for streaming return to `AsyncIterator[ChatChunk]` where ChatChunk has Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] delta and Optional[str] text. That avoids index-on-union. Does runtime already create objects we can wrap?

arun: Runtime yields dicts and str. We can normalise in the streamer to always yield a small dataclass-like object (or a Pydantic model) with attributes. That's a runtime and stub coordinated change but should be backwards-compatible for most users if we keep the old iterator semantics (still yields same data) but types improve.

rachel: Would this break code that does `if isinstance(chunk, str): ...` ? Maybe, but we can keep `.text` set for text chunks and keep `is_text()` helper.

priya: Also note pyright flagged that editor completions are gone because blob is `Any` in some stubs; moving to explicit ChatChunk will help.

tom: Ok plan: 1) change stub return type for chat.stream to `AsyncIterator[ChatChunk]` plus add ChatChunk typedclass/TypedDict with `.delta: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]]` and `.text: Optional[str]`, 2) runtime: normalise yields to instances of a tiny dataclass (fast, no pydantic), 3) add unit + mypy test and a sampleapp snippet showing attribute access.

arun: I'll open an issue and assign eng-ml for autogen template change. Also will add a deprecation note: we should keep a tiny compatibility shim so `isinstance(chunk, str)` still works for a release cycle or provide `.raw` property.

rachel: Thanks. Can you also add a quick VSCode snippet to the docs so users see how to migrate streaming loops? New hires hit this in onboarding.

devx-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3190 by @arun :white_check_mark:

priya: I'll volunteer to review the PR and sanity-check perf impact of object creation in hot loops. We should microbenchmark.

tom: Good point. If object allocation is a worry we can keep yielding raw primitives and have a helper `chat.wrap_chunk(chunk)` that returns ChatChunk (explicit opt-in). But DX will be worse. Need perf numbers.

rachel: For now let's aim for the wrapper but also ship a microbenchmark and a fallback opt-in for raw streaming for users who care about minimal allocations.

arun: I'll draft the PR with both options: default ergonomic wrapper + `raw=True` opt-out on stream() to yield original primitives. Will include tests and sampleapp changes.

rachel: Awesome, that should make the typing story much nicer. Thanks everyone :sparkles:
